definition: A training strategy that presents training examples to a model in a meaningful order, typically progressing from easier to harder examples.
details: Curriculum learning is inspired by how humans often learn, and has been shown in some settings to speed up training convergence and improve final model performance.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. And that is Curriculum Learning — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
